intro: You are standing on Alişar Höyük, a mound near Yozgat, in Yozgat province. Its story stretches from the 4th millennium BC to the 1st millennium BC, and in the Iron Age it is thought to have belonged to the land of Tabal.
history: Beneath your feet lie layers of unbroken life. The mound has been occupied continuously since the 4th millennium BC, and it was an important centre in Hittite and Phrygian times. Its modern story begins with Erich Schmidt, whose excavations of 1927–32 rank among the pioneering campaigns of Anatolian archaeology.
structure-1: Now you are looking at the citadel, the most protected and elevated part of a city or fortress. Pause here for a moment and imagine looking out from the heights over everything below.
structure-2: Below the citadel lies the Lower Town, the settlement where houses and workshops stood. Picture the daily bustle of the people who lived and worked here.
structure-4: Here you see building remains: traces of various rooms and spaces that survive in the ancient city. Each line of wall is a clue to how people once arranged their lives.
structure-5: Now follow the street layout, the network of streets and roads that survives in the ancient city. Walk it slowly, and you trace routes its people once took.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the fortifications, and take a moment there to imagine the mound as its defenders once saw it.
facts: Did you know? The distinctive pottery known as 'Alişar ware' gives its name to the 'Alişar IV' period in archaeology. Excavated between 1927 and 1932, this mound is where the chronology of Anatolian archaeology was first built, and for a long time other digs dated themselves against it. Hattian, Assyrian trading-colony and Hittite layers sit one atop another here: three worlds in a single hill.
outro: This brings our journey through Alişar Höyük to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
